mohit: Heads-up — bringing Nightingale13B (int4) up on staging and hitting a weird token-frame wrap in long-context tests. Repro below, small seed.

mohit: repro command: ```./redwood-eval --model nightingale13b-int4 --prompt-file tests/longctx_prompts.json --max-tokens 2048 --use-kvcache --quant int4```

mohit: symptoms: after ~1200 tokens, continuation starts repeating a short phrase and attention logs show kv-cache keys/values reading from earlier positions (looks like a frame shift). No crashes, just semantic drift.

emily: have you tried comparing tokenizer ids with the upstream nightingale tokenizer? could be an off-by-one or sentinel token mapping.

mohit: yes — token ids line up for first 800 tokens. Dumped the token stream and compared; there's a consistent +3 offset in later chunks relative to model's kv-index.

yuri: +3 offset smells like a block/reorder issue. Are we using headwise rotary (per-head) or shared rotary table? Nightingale uses per-head phase params AFAICT.

mohit: runtime selected per-head rotary kernel. Model file metadata says "rotary_mode: headwise" and head_dim=64.

emily: also check tokenizer special tokens: if model uses a custom BOS/EOS and we switch to standard, that could shift kv indices when caching prefixes.

mohit: good call — tokenizer has an extra <pad_sentinel> mapped to id 50256 in this file, whereas our standard maps to 1. But I thought that only affects initial offset.

ci-bot: deploy-note: staging/nightingale13b-int4 rollup finished at 7012345672 by infra-deploy. Tests: unit=ok, smoke=fail(longctx-repetition).

james: can you paste the kvcache index dump around the drift point? a small table with (time idx -> token id -> head offset) would help.

mohit: pasted a truncated dump: ```kvcache[1196..1206]: [(1196->4261),(1197->17),(1198->412),(1199->4261),(1200->4261),(1201->17)] then at 1204 reads indices [1201,1202,1203] but token ids correspond to [1198,1199,1200]```


yuri: that looks like a write/read mismatch: writes are using absolute positions but reads use modulo by block size incorrectly. What's the batch/block size? maybe 64 vs 128 mismatch.

mohit: runtime uses block_size=128 for batching, but the model metadata (export) lists kv_block=64. I didn't expect that to matter because runtime should override, but maybe conversion left an embedded stride.

emily: try forcing runtime to use kv_block=64 (config flag) and rerun. If it fixes, downstream conversion needs patch.

mohit: ran with `--kv-block 64` and longctx drift disappears in quick smoke. Streaming looks stable. So conversion left an internal stride marker that our kernel picked up.

james: nice isolate. Two follow-ups: 1) add a unit test that converts Nightingale exports and validates kv_block in generated runtime config, 2) add a defensive check in runtime that verifies model kv_block <= runtime max_block and warns/fails if mismatch.

sara: also run a quantization parity check: compare logits at 512 token increments between fp16 and int4 to ensure no additional drift introduced by quant. If int4 shows compounding error correlated with block mismatch, we need to alert quant team.

mohit: did fp16 vs int4 parity: fp16 stable, int4 shows larger variance but only when block mismatch is present. After forcing kv-block=64 int4 parity matches baseline within expected epsilon.

yuri: conclusion: conversion pipeline writes kv_block=64 into model file, runtime autodetect picks block_size=128 based on host GPU throughput heuristics, but the kvcache writer/reader code wasn't normalizing between the two. We'll make runtime prefer model-declared kv_block where present and expose override with warning.

emily: add a small migration script to sanitize older exports that may carry wrong kv_block metadata. Plenty of exported models in S3 could be impacted.

mohit: I'll open a PR: 1) runtime defensive check + opt-in override flag, 2) export sanitizer to rewrite kv_block field, 3) unit tests and nightly on-nightingale int4 smoke. Assigning to me for patch, emily for sanitizer review, yuri for kernel sanity check.

mohit: estimated time: patch + tests ~1 working day. Rolling to prod after CI and a short canary for 24h.

james: also add a short note in the onboarding checklist to validate kv_block vs runtime block size during model bring-up.

emily: 👍 and add an eval that runs the int4 fp16 parity every 1k tokens so we can catch regressions early.

mohit: thanks folks — will post PR link and sample diff here once ready. :party_parrot:
